prompt.context: You have just been appointed Chief of Health Reforms and have discovered that kidney dialysis is a major portion of public health care expenditures.
prompt.question: What analytical techniques do you use to determine if this cost can be reduced?

framework: Determine whether high costs stem from high incidence of kidney disorders, high cost per procedure, or both
Assess whether unscrupulous practices are shifting costs onto the public health budget
Compare national incidence rates with other countries to benchmark and identify policy levers
Analyze cost components of the procedure (professional fees, consumables, capital equipment)

questions.prompt: Is the high expenditure driven by incidence, procedure cost, or both?
questions.guidance: Candidate should decompose total expenditure into: Total Cost = (Number of patients) x (Cost per procedure x Frequency). Investigating each driver separately—whether more people need dialysis or whether each treatment is expensive—is the core analytical split.

questions.prompt: Are unscrupulous practitioners inflating costs on the public budget?
questions.guidance: Compare the proportion of kidney dialysis cases funded by public versus private health insurance. A disproportionately high share on the public budget may indicate providers are steering patients toward the public payer.

questions.prompt: Is the incidence of kidney disorder in this country unusually high compared with other countries?
questions.guidance: Benchmark national kidney disorder incidence rates against comparable countries. If the rate is higher, investigate whether public-health policy interventions or awareness campaigns could reduce incidence, especially among groups typically covered by public funds (the poor, the elderly).

questions.prompt: What factors drive higher incidence among publicly insured populations?
questions.guidance: Build a regression or statistical model to identify factors most correlated with kidney treatment need. Focus on demographics covered by public insurance (low-income, elderly). Evaluate feasibility of preventative programs targeting these groups.

questions.prompt: If the cost per procedure is high, what are the component drivers?
questions.guidance: Break procedure cost into: (1) Professional fees — consider capping government reimbursement rates; (2) Consumables — explore newer, lower-cost materials or technologies; (3) Capital equipment — evaluate newer technologies that reduce per-treatment equipment costs.

recommendation: Focus cost-reduction efforts on the two main levers: reducing incidence through preventative public-health programs for high-risk groups, and lowering cost-per-procedure by capping professional fees and adopting cost-efficient technologies
Conduct an audit comparing public vs. private billing patterns to detect any fraudulent or unscrupulous cost-shifting
risks: Incidence reduction programs take time before yielding savings; short-term budget pressure remains
Fee caps may reduce provider participation, affecting patient access
Technology investment requires upfront capital before generating savings
next_steps: Benchmark incidence rates against peer countries and segment by payer type
Commission a regression analysis on demographic risk factors for kidney disease
Pilot a preventative care program for high-risk publicly insured populations
Engage independent auditors to review public vs. private billing ratios
